reason: Checked on the operator's ask; the 06:00 run had already scored it 44 (ranking 36). Suniva is the oldest US-owned merchant maker of monocrystalline solar cells (Norcross, Georgia, 1 GW). On 9 Sep 2026 it completed an $835M raise to build a 4.5 GW cell plant in Laurens County, South Carolina (operations from Q2 2027; 5.5 GW total) - senior secured facilities from Goldman Sachs Alternatives and I Squared Capital, a second-lien facility from JBA Asset Management, equity from Electron Capital, Orion Infrastructure Capital and Rubric Capital. That is project finance for a factory, not a growth round that funds brand-building - the Joulent pattern. The identity moment is real but not yet here: a reverse merger with Nasdaq-listed SUNation Energy (SUNE), announced 8 Jun 2026, Suniva holders ~98.2% and SUNation ~1.8%, the combined company to trade as Suniva; closing targeted H2 2026 subject to stockholder votes, S-4 effectiveness and Nasdaq clearance, none found completed as of 15 Sep. Leadership: Tony Etnyre CEO, Matt Card President and COO, Didric Cederholm Chairman; no marketing or brand function found; no motorsport tie for any of them. A B2B cell supplier whose customers are module makers has no sponsorship audience, and SUNation's consumer installer business (NY, FL, HI) is 1.8% of the combination. Honest pillars: timing 14, capacity 9, brand fit 12 (US-made solar is FE-shaped on paper), urgency 10, ops fit 4 = 49. Re-open when the merger closes AND the listed company stands up a marketing function or a consumer brand push; until then it is a manufacturer with a plant to build.
